title: HyFunc: Accelerating LLM-based Function Calls for Agentic AI through Hybrid-Model Cascade and Dynamic Templating

problem.claim: LLM-based translation of user intent into structured function calls has computational redundancy and high inference latency, hindering real-time applications.

contributions.claim: HyFunc uses a hybrid-model cascade in which a large model produces a soft token for function retrieval and smaller-model generation of the final call.
HyFunc uses dynamic templating to inject boilerplate parameter syntax during generation within an extended vLLM engine.
HyFunc is evaluated on the unseen BFCL benchmark to assess potential generalization limitations.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present HyFunc as a novel framework that systematically eliminates the identified inefficiencies.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report an inference latency of 0.828 seconds, outperforming all baseline models.
The authors report performance of 80.1%, surpassing models with a comparable parameter scale.
The authors state that the code is publicly available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Agentic AI function calling suffers from computational redundancy and latency.
The paper identifies redundant function-description processing, large-model full-sequence generation, and boilerplate syntax generation.
HyFunc combines a hybrid-model cascade with dynamic templating to reduce these redundancies.
The framework is evaluated on the unseen BFCL benchmark.
The authors report improved latency and performance relative to stated baselines and comparable-scale models.

source_observation.claim: The approach separates intent distillation, function retrieval, final-call generation, and boilerplate syntax insertion across specialized mechanisms.

interpretation.claim: Decomposing predictable and semantically demanding parts of structured generation may reduce unnecessary computation.

application.claim: Use staged model specialization and runtime templating when structured outputs contain both semantic decisions and predictable syntax.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how the approach behaves outside the evaluated benchmark or under function distributions unlike BFCL.

unknowns: Baseline identities and experimental configuration are not specified.
Model architectures, parameter counts, training data, and tuning procedures are not specified.
The abstract does not report variance, statistical significance, or hardware details.
The scope and composition of BFCL are not described.
